name: New York: From Trading Post to Skyline
description: How a Dutch trading post at the mouth of the Hudson grew into a harbour, a stock market, a skyline and a stage for artists and ideas.

checkpoints.name: Hudson's river
checkpoints.note: Henry Hudson sailed up the river that now bears his name in 1609. The Dutch founded a trading post that became New York City, and the port grew under English rule.

checkpoints.name: Harbour, canal and bridge
checkpoints.note: The Erie Canal tied the port to the Great Lakes. The New York Times began in 1851, Central Park was laid out, Edison's Pearl Street Station lit part of Manhattan, and the Brooklyn Bridge and Statue of Liberty arrived.

checkpoints.name: Towers and the crash
checkpoints.note: The Harlem Renaissance flowered, The New Yorker started, and the Chrysler Building and Empire State Building rose. Babe Ruth made the Yankees famous. The Wall Street crash of 1929 shook the world, and the 1939 World's Fair showed visions of the future.

checkpoints.name: Capital of postwar culture
checkpoints.note: The United Nations made its home in the city. Jackson Pollock and Abstract Expressionism, then Andy Warhol and Pop art, put New York at the centre of art. Jackie Robinson played for the Brooklyn Dodgers, and the Stonewall riots took place in 1969.

checkpoints.name: Towers, art and tragedy
checkpoints.note: The twin towers of the World Trade Center opened in the early 1970s. Jean-Michel Basquiat painted, and Seinfeld was set in the city. The towers were destroyed in the attacks of September 11, 2001.
